questions.q: Why would Northbridge prefer Ingress over a separate LoadBalancer Service for each public-facing app?
options: Ingress is required by Kubernetes for any external traffic
A LoadBalancer Service per app means a separate, billed external load balancer for each one, while Ingress routes many hosts/paths through one shared entry point
LoadBalancer Services cannot route HTTP traffic at all
Ingress replaces the need for Services entirely
questions.explain: Ingress multiplexes host- and path-based routing for many services behind a single shared external IP, avoiding a separate cloud load balancer per app.

questions.q: What is the actual relationship between an Ingress resource and an Ingress Controller?
options: They are the same thing with two names
The Ingress resource is a declared set of routing rules; the Ingress Controller is the component that reads those rules and actually proxies traffic
The Ingress Controller is optional and traffic routes without one
The Ingress resource runs as a Pod on every node
questions.explain: An Ingress object on its own does nothing — it's a declaration of intent. An Ingress Controller (e.g. ingress-nginx) watches Ingress resources and configures a real proxy to match.

questions.q: In an Ingress rule, what does pathType: Prefix do differently from pathType: Exact?
options: Prefix matches any URL beginning with the given path; Exact requires a precise, full match
Prefix only works with HTTPS; Exact only works with HTTP
They behave identically in all cases
Exact matches any URL beginning with the given path; Prefix requires a precise match
questions.explain: Prefix path matching matches any URL starting with the specified path segment, while Exact requires the URL to match precisely.

questions.q: Northbridge installs two different Ingress Controllers in the same cluster. What field on an Ingress resource ensures the right controller acts on a given set of rules?
options: metadata.name
spec.tls
spec.ingressClassName
spec.rules.host
questions.explain: ingressClassName ties an Ingress resource to a specific IngressClass/controller, removing ambiguity when multiple controllers are installed.

questions.q: Where does TLS termination typically happen for Northbridge's public-facing services behind an Ingress?
options: Inside every individual backend Pod, which must each manage its own certificate
At the Ingress Controller, which decrypts HTTPS using a certificate from a Secret and forwards plain HTTP internally
Inside the Service object's spec.tls field
TLS cannot be used with Ingress
questions.explain: The Ingress Controller terminates TLS at the edge using a certificate referenced via secretName, then forwards unencrypted HTTP to the backend Service — so individual backends don't need their own TLS setup.
